mappings.note: Part (a) is the definition and the reason for ignoring detail (LO-7); part (b) makes the student sort kept from ignored against the specific question the cricket model answers (LO-8).
Both halves are LO-3: the mask as a real problem needing several branches, and then the explicit question of why branches exist if nature has no boundaries.
Part (a) is SI units and the cost of mixing them (LO-6); part (b) is mathematics as a language expressing relationships (LO-7). The two halves map to two different outcomes of the same competency.
Both halves are estimation - why a rough figure is worth having and how the calorie example builds intuition, which is LO-9's reasonableness and cross-check purpose.

Part (a) debunks by asking what measurable mechanism could exist (LO-6); part (b) explicitly asks what this shows about the value of scientific thinking, which is LO-4's 'where scientific thinking applies outside science'.
Three parts all on the one model - how it was simplified and what the simplification explained, LO-7. Part (a) is only biographical framing and carries no separate outcome.
Part (a) is revisability as new evidence arrives (LO-5); part (b) is specifically how a failure advances science, which is LO-8's re-examination rather than dismissal.
Part (a) is everyday words carrying narrow scientific meanings (C7.1-LO-6); part (b) is the historical and agreed origin of a symbol (C5.2-LO-6). The two halves belong to different competencies.
Ravi's balloon rocket is named as a model (LO-7), and the discards - paint, logos - are justified by their irrelevance to the launch question he is answering (LO-8).
A kilogram-versus-pound failure (LO-6) set entirely in commerce, with the answer resting on fairness and consistency in trade - which is what earns LO-4 here and not for the laboratory unit items.
Priya's error is the everyday sense of 'theory' as a guess (LO-6); Mr Sharma's correction is the law-versus-theory discrimination, including that one does not become the other (LO-4).
Harish is credited with attempting a prediction but without the reasoning a prediction needs (LO-7); the neighbour's remedy is to frame specific measurable questions, which is LO-6.
A per-person-per-day rate scaled by people and days, used to reject an implausible figure - LO-9's estimate-and-cross-check in full.
One sea wall requiring physics, chemistry, biology and mathematics from four experts - the clearest instance in the chapter of LO-3's real problem needing more than one branch.
Part (a) is symbol-to-quantity recall (C5.2-LO-6); part (b) argues symbols beat everyday words because those are ambiguous, which is C7.1-LO-6's precision claim carried over to notation.

A student applying scientific thinking to a viral rumour outside any science lesson is LO-4; the method - looking for a mechanism and refusing to judge by popularity - is LO-6's measurable-evidence test.
The coach's formula is defended as a compact statement of how speed, distance and time relate rather than as arithmetic - C5.2-LO-7 exactly. No unit convention is at issue, so LO-6 stays out.

The nature-walk case study asks for both symbols separately: compass gives asking the right testable questions (LO-6) and choosing models while knowing their limits (LO-7); the magnifying-glass part falls back to the inquiry competency, as no outcome names observation. Partly weak fit.
